items.title: Add a branch on housing finance under climate repricing
items.why: Likely the next strongest extension of the insurance cluster.

items.title: Collect more direct evidence on care-worker migration regimes
items.why: Would either strengthen or narrow note SS-003.

items.title: Research civil anti-drone governance for non-military infrastructure
items.why: Would sharpen the spillover claim in SS-006.

items.title: Track procurement-level adoption of provenance requirements
items.why: Critical for deciding whether SS-005 remains canon-worthy.

items.title: Stress-test the new observability branch against actual policy programs
items.why: Would show whether SS-008 is a durable canon note or just a temporary synthesis convenience.

items.title: Gather evidence on geolocation-heavy trade regimes beyond deforestation compliance
items.why: Needed before SS-904 can be promoted from quarantine.

items.title: Track recovery, exclusion, and over-requesting risk in wallet-mediated proof systems
items.why: SS-009 strengthens the canon only if threshold proofs scale without producing intolerable civic lockout or coercive data collection.

items.title: Track delegated-act rollout and customs integration for product passports
items.why: SS-010 is strongest if object passports become operational market-access infrastructure rather than symbolic transparency layers.

items.title: Track when eInvoicing rails are reused outside tax
items.why: SS-011 is strongest if structured transaction data becomes shared infrastructure for customs, procurement, trade finance, or sustainability reporting rather than staying a tax-only compliance layer.

items.title: Track court treatment and cross-border recognition of electronic originals
items.why: SS-012 is strongest if exclusive digital control survives real disputes involving insolvency, customs, and conflict-of-laws friction rather than remaining a legislative or pilot-layer success.

items.title: Track uptake of machine-verifiable organisational authority in filings, payments, and procurement
items.why: SS-013 is strongest if role credentials and mandate proofs escape pilots and actually replace emailed delegation, uploaded authority letters, or bespoke portal permissions.

items.title: Track whether once-only evidence exchange escapes EU cross-border edge cases
items.why: SS-014 is strongest if authoritative-source retrieval reshapes ordinary administrative and regulated workflows rather than remaining a special-purpose interoperability layer.

items.title: Track whether relay-provider status becomes a reusable cross-domain chokepoint
items.why: SS-015 is strongest if certified access points, qualified trust service providers, and registered intermediaries become real admissibility infrastructure rather than optional plumbing.

items.title: Track whether live standing checks become ordinary admissibility infrastructure
items.why: SS-016 is strongest if trusted lists, revocation feeds, capability directories, and registry confirmations become runtime conditions of use rather than optional implementation details.

items.title: Track whether special large-load classes become durable utility governance
items.why: SS-017 is strongest if large-load tariffs, minimum obligations, flexibility commitments, and self-supply expectations spread beyond a few headline proceedings and become a normal response to system-shaping demand.

items.title: Track whether travel preclearance becomes normal mobility infrastructure
items.why: SS-018 is strongest if upstream authorisation, carrier enforcement, and digital travel credentials materially change boarding practice and border operations rather than remaining a patchwork of traveller-facing apps and isolated programmes.

items.title: Track whether electronic prior authorization becomes real care-access infrastructure
items.why: SS-019 is strongest if prior-auth APIs, metrics, and provider-side workflow integration materially change scheduling, specialty economics, and patient access rather than merely digitising an old annoyance.

items.title: Track whether digital work-right checks become normal labour-market gatekeeping
items.why: SS-020 is strongest if employers, platforms, staffing firms, and cross-border service chains actually reorganise onboarding around digital permission and declaration stacks rather than keeping them as marginal compliance tools.

items.title: Track whether permit-ready models become normal approval infrastructure
items.why: SS-021 is strongest if machine-checkable BIM/GIS submissions, rule libraries, and validation tooling materially change approval throughput rather than remaining a pilot or premium-capability layer.

items.title: Track whether payee verification expands into aliases, wallets, and cross-border non-bank payment flows
items.why: Would show whether SS-022 is a durable broad branch or still mostly a bank-transfer phenomenon.

items.title: Track whether telemetry-conditioned extraction rights spread beyond water and fisheries
items.why: SS-023 is strongest if approved meters, electronic monitoring, and upload cadence become a reusable governance pattern across other regulated take regimes rather than staying domain-local.

items.title: Track whether insurers, mortgagees, and public backstops start explicitly co-governing housing finance
items.why: SS-024 is strongest if insurability becomes a durable collateral-admissibility layer rather than a temporary affordability shock.

items.title: Track whether listing-time lodging legality spreads beyond tourist rentals
items.why: SS-025 is strongest if registration-number governance, platform verification, and disablement orders spread into adjacent occupancy markets rather than remaining a small set of tourist-city exceptions.
